title: Python async (asyncio), Part 1: build your own event loop
tldr: Why a gateway that asks 5 sellers one after another takes 1,450 ms, what one thread per waiting call costs (measured), and concurrency vs parallelism. Then generators (yield, send, throw, close, yield from), native coroutines (async def, await, the __await__ protocol, never-awaited coroutines) and a toy event loop built step by step: a ready queue, a timer heap and a scheduler. Gateway v1 on the toy loop overlaps the waits (900 ms on one thread) and cuts at a 250 ms budget; then what the toy loop gets wrong: blocking calls, 10 times the load, no real I/O, exceptions and forgotten awaits. Ends with threads vs loops vs asyncio and an interview drill.
